name: Ward L. Lambert Fieldhouse and Gymnasium

references.provider: Purdue University Archives and Special Collections, Purdue Campus Facilities and Buildings Historic Database
references.source_date: Historical record for the 1937 building; retrieved page describes original construction
references.use: Describes stone, brick, steel and reinforced concrete, a one-story fieldhouse, a four-story gymnasium section, and original dimensions. It supports the material and multilevel institutional character; the source does not document the current roof profile, facade dimensions, truss spacing, or whether the historic entrance tower remains today.

references.provider: Boston Public Library Tichnor Brothers postcard collection, via Wikimedia Commons
references.use: Historical visual reference for brick massing, horizontal window bands, pale stone accents, and a prominent entrance tower. Exact proportions are not measured; tower survival in current conditions is unverified.

references.provider: Tripadvisor visitor photo on Lambert Fieldhouse listing
references.source_date: Associated review dated 2024-09; photo capture date unspecified
references.use: Contemporary visual cue for red brick, tall light-colored concrete pilasters, and large block-like glazing; dimensions and exact bay rhythm are not measured.

references.provider: Dave Wegiel Photography, Gene Edmonds Invitational at Lambert Fieldhouse
references.use: Interior visual reference for the arched steel-roof volume, upper spectator/official balconies, and event display/equipment cues. The new truss spacing, balcony extents, and generic display remain illustrative.

references.provider: Purdue University Athletics, Lambert Fieldhouse facility page
references.use: Official identity and current six-lane, 200 m track use.

references.provider: Purdue University ArcGIS BuildingShapesZip4 layer 0, feature 261
references.source_crs: WGS84 geographic coordinates in the retained raw snapshot; transformed by the project local approximate conversion
references.use: Preserved plan footprint and exact segmented exterior wall alignment; the new horizontal bands follow its ten unique perimeter edges. It does not verify height, roof, tower, or facade style.

references.provider: Purdue University Archives and Special Collections, Purdue Campus Facilities and Buildings Historic Database
references.source_date: Historical record for 1937 construction; page retrieved 2026-10-24
references.use: Source-supported plan dimensions/story count: one-story 172 x 303 ft fieldhouse plus separate four-story 110 x 210 ft gymnasium section. The record does not localize/orient those volumes against current GIS and gives no measured roof profile, elevations, facade cadence, or current tower status. Dimensions were converted using 0.3048 m/ft.

references.provider: Purdue University ArcGIS BuildingShapesZip4 layer 0, feature 261
references.source_crs: WGS84 geographic; project local approximate conversion X=(lon+86.9137)*84810.6042 m, Y=(lat-40.4274)*111040 m
references.use: The saved project footprint mesh reproduces the source polygon and is U-shaped with 20 boundary edges. It constrains the outer plan and facade band positions, but does not identify the roofed fieldhouse/gym allocation or verify height.

measurement_and_frame.measurement_method: Average paired inner/outer boundary vertices at each sample station to recover the lane-one centerline polygon and sum its closed polygon edges in local meters.
measurement_and_frame.placement: Local origin, GIS footprint, and track mesh preserved. The internal volumes are placed as an illustrative hypothesis because the archive does not georegister them and the U-shaped GIS footprint does not fully resolve the roofed area.

stone_band_registration.method: Extract the 20-edge closed GIS perimeter cycle from the bottom boundary edges of the saved ground-footprint mesh; orient each rectangular band segment to its edge tangent; position its center 0.20 m outward along the edge normal.
stone_band_registration.pier_check: 33 existing pier centers compared to nearest GIS segment; mean distance 0.03296 m, maximum 0.10587 m.

volume_plan_dimensions_from_archive.story_height: not measured; four-level envelope in the model is schematic

uncertainties: The historical record gives two plan rectangles and story counts but does not georegister them. Current hall/gym placement, orientation, and connection are illustrative and remain a source conflict with parts of the U-shaped GIS outline.

Fieldhouse roof curvature, eave/ridge heights, steel member sections/spacing, gym overall elevation, and floor-to-floor heights are not measured. The gym height is only a schematic four-level envelope.
Facade window cadence and detail are visually estimated from historical/contemporary imagery; stone band positions follow GIS edges, but the historic photos do not supply elevation dimensions.
The historic entrance tower is hidden from current model views. The postcard supports only a historical tower depiction; current survival/location/proportions remain unverified.
Balcony extents, scoreboard, interior seating, event layout, and gym circulation/floor plates remain schematic; no accessibility or as-built claim is inferred.
GIS feature 261 is an approximate plan source, not a surveyed wall/roof edge; the project local conversion is approximate and does not independently verify the building’s height or interior.
changes_since_round5: Resized the arched one-story hall roof to Purdue Archives dimensions: 303 x 172 ft (92.354 x 52.426 m). Roof curvature/eave height remain schematic; the archival plan dimensions are documented, but their local position/orientation is not registered by the source.

Added a visually distinct four-story gym volume with archive plan dimensions 210 x 110 ft (64.008 x 33.528 m), a flat roof, three upper glazing rows, transparent ground-floor storefront, brick piers/spandrels and illustrative floor plates. Four-level envelope height and window spacing are estimates.

Rebuilt the pale stone facade bands against the actual 20-edge boundary extracted from the saved GIS footprint mesh. Each band segment is oriented along its source edge and positioned 0.20 m outward; the max computed center-offset error is about 0.000002 m. Existing 33 facade piers remain near the footprint (mean center distance 0.033 m; max 0.106 m).
Replaced previous roof-support detailing with trusses fitted to the reduced hall span. Truss size/spacing remain schematic and are visible in the cutaway render.
Renamed and hid the historic postcard entrance-tower pieces from current model views. They are retained only as a historical conjecture; no claim is made that the tower survives today.

Added plan/section overlay to compare archive dimensions against GIS feature 261. It shows that the GIS outline is U-shaped and does not uniquely register the documented volumes; parts of the projected hall rectangle cross notched/open areas. This is disclosed as unresolved rather than treated as verified geometry.

Saved and reopened the source library, rendered exterior and interior views, verified no unmaterialed meshes/material-output errors, and remeasured the unchanged six-lane track centerline at 199.988956721 m.
